brief: The world's strongest coffee, as advertised. Beans, grounds, cold brew cans. Our buyers are heavy coffee drinkers who like a bit of humor.

profile.business_summary: DTC coffee brand selling high-caffeine beans, grounds, and cold brew cans targeted at heavy coffee drinkers who appreciate humor.
profile.product: High-caffeine coffee (beans, grounds, and cold brew cans)

relevant_tags.why: The core product is coffee, which is a beverage.
Coffee is a daily consumable grocery item.
Coffee beans and grounds are standard pantry staples.
High-caffeine coffee functions as an energy and performance booster.
Cold brew cans offer quick, ready-to-drink convenience.

persona_conflicts.evidence: The brand's positioning as 'the world's strongest coffee' combined with a humorous tone may be perceived as a novelty or gimmick by strict wellness optimizers.

persona_conflicts.conflict: disinterested_in trendy language and loud aesthetics
persona_conflicts.evidence: An intense, high-caffeine coffee brand utilizing humor conflicts with the understated, heritage, and quality-focused preferences of the Affluent Classic.

note_signals.why: Late-night traffic spikes and impulse-friendly convenience buyers align well with ready-to-drink cold brew cans.
Conservative brand sensibility and high-AOV focus will likely clash with a loud, humorous, high-caffeine coffee brand.
Audience responds best to a fun, playful brand voice, which aligns perfectly with the advertiser's humorous angle.
Beverage-focused audience seeking indulgence is highly compatible with premium, high-strength coffee.

profile.gate_reason: The product and target audience are clearly defined, allowing us to proceed with onboarding and placement planning.
clarifying_questions: What is your average price point or AOV?
Do you offer a subscription option for your coffee products, or is it primarily one-time purchases?
Are there specific demographic groups (e.g., age, gender) you target beyond heavy coffee drinkers?

assumptions: Price not given; assumed $60 for a 'unknown' product.
repeat_consumable: assumed 2.5 orders per customer over ~6 months.
No target CPA/ROAS or margin given; assumed 50% gross margin (typical for beverages). Give a target CPA to replace this.
Target CPA = 70% of max affordable CAC ($60 x 50% margin x 2.5 orders = $75.00).

pricing.rationale: Acquisition goal with no conversion history: pay per click. Max CPC = target CPA $52.50 x click-to-purchase rate (1.6%-5.6% for beverages). Clicks are observable without trusting a pixel, so both sides can verify billing.
pricing.tcpa_unlock: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded; until then Disco can't predict conversion rate for this brand.

budget.pacing: even daily pacing; pause a host if CPA > 2.0x target after 150 clicks

allocations.rationale: score 0.28 -> relative fit x1.40 on CTR/CVR; max bid $2.35 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%
score 0.27 -> relative fit x1.38 on CTR/CVR; max bid $2.32 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%
score 0.24 -> relative fit x1.29 on CTR/CVR; max bid $2.17 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%
score 0.22 -> relative fit x1.25 on CTR/CVR; max bid $2.09 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%

warnings: No budget given: recommending $3,150, the smallest budget that buys 300 clicks per host.

phases.name: learning
phases.rule: bid = start bid per host (70% of break-even); pacing adjustment only
phases.why: stable bids so measured CTR/CVR aren't confounded by bid changes

phases.name: enhanced_cpc
phases.until: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded; until then Disco can't predict conversion rate for this brand.
phases.rule: bid = start bid x conversion_likelihood x pacing, clamped to [floor, max bid]
phases.why: spend more on shoppers who look likely to buy, never above break-even

phases.name: target_cpa
phases.rule: Disco bids automatically to hit $52.50 CPA
phases.why: only once Disco can predict this brand's conversion rate

adjustments.reason: Bid higher when the shopper looks like a high converter: their persona match for this campaign vs the host's average shopper (from the serve-time persona posterior).
Under-delivering vs the daily plan -> bid up a little; over-delivering -> bid down.

bid_strategy.rationale: Start below break-even and fixed so the first two weeks measure the hosts, not the bidder; then bid per shopper within a hard ceiling (max CPC = target CPA x CVR), so a single click can never cost more than it's expected to earn.
